title: JSON Syntax Doctor
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Python for Robotics
description: Judge six short JSON settings files against five JSON rules: mark the line that breaks a rule and name the rule, or decide that the file is valid. Used in Chapter 1.

educational.topic: The five syntax rules of the JSON file format
learningObjectives: Critique six short JSON settings files by marking the line that breaks a JSON rule and naming the rule, or by judging the file correct, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Judge each file against five explicit rules and commit a line and a rule; one valid file tests whether the learner can decide that nothing is wrong
keyQuestions: Which of the five rules does this line break?
Why does a missing comma belong to the line above the one where the parser complains?
How do you decide that a file has no error at all?
commonMisconceptions: Single quotes work in JSON as they do in Python
A trailing comma is harmless, as in Python lists
Comments starting with # or // are allowed
JSON booleans are spelled True and False
A file that looks unusual must be wrong
assessmentOpportunities: Six committed judgments, one attempt each, line and rule both required; 5 of 6 for mastery

controls.label: Click a line of the file or the No error box, then click a rule
Check / Next file / See score / Try again
